# llms.txt — PACT

> PACT is conditional settlement infrastructure for the agent economy: money moves
> only when an independent verifier confirms a delivery meets the buyer's
> acceptance criteria. Funds are held in PayPal escrow (`intent=AUTHORIZE`) before
> work starts and released with `capture`, or returned with `void`. It is
> guest-first — a public deployment provisions an isolated workspace with no
> account — and runs on PayPal **Sandbox** by design.

This file is the compact, machine-oriented entry point to PACT's canonical
documentation. It follows the [llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org/) convention. A longer
consolidated version is at [`llms-full.txt`](https://github.com/itzebe/pact/blob/master/llms-full.txt). The full documentation
index is [`docs/README.md`](https://github.com/itzebe/pact/blob/master/docs/README.md) and the navigation map is
[`docs/knowledge-map.md`](https://github.com/itzebe/pact/blob/master/docs/knowledge-map.md).

This file is served verbatim at <https://pact-flame.vercel.app/llms.txt>; the links
below are repository-relative so they resolve on GitHub, and each is also reachable
from the live site.

- **Repository:** https://github.com/itzebe/pact
- **Live application:** https://pact-flame.vercel.app/
- **Health endpoint:** https://pact-flame.vercel.app/api/health
- **Default branch:** `master`
- **License:** MIT
- **Language:** Python (FastAPI backend) + JavaScript (React/Vite frontend)

## What PACT is

Two parties — an autonomous buyer agent and competing seller agents — agree to a
small, well-specified deliverable. PACT holds the buyer's funds in PayPal escrow
before any work starts, an independent verifier checks the delivery against each
acceptance criterion, and only then does the money move: `capture` on a pass,
`void` on a fail. Every transition is recorded in a hash-chained ledger.

PACT is **not** a generic payment gateway and does **not** move real money in the
demo. The live deployment is configured for the PayPal **Sandbox** host.

## Primary purpose

Provide a neutral, verifiable settlement layer for agent-to-agent work so that two
strangers can transact without either being able to cheat the other: the seller
cannot be paid for undelivered work, and the buyer cannot withhold payment for work
that was delivered and verified.

## Who it serves

- **Autonomous agents** that hire and pay each other for small deliverables.
- **Developers** building agent marketplaces that need a settlement primitive.
- **Researchers and evaluators** who need a runnable, auditable reference
  implementation of conditional (escrow) settlement on fiat rails.

## Verified capabilities

Each is implemented and covered by tests in this repository (see
[`docs/implementation-status.md`](https://github.com/itzebe/pact/blob/master/docs/implementation-status.md) for the evidence):

- Guest-first isolated sessions (server-provisioned, cookie + CSRF).
- Job creation with a brief, acceptance criteria, and a hard budget ceiling.
- Multi-round seller negotiation with an in-code budget guardrail.
- PayPal escrow: order → buyer approval → authorization (hold) → capture | void.
- Delivery production by a seller agent and independent verification.
- Partial and full refunds of a captured payment.
- PayPal webhook signature verification and exactly-once event processing.
- Hash-chained, tamper-evident audit ledger (`verify_chain`).
- Durable, instance-safe PostgreSQL persistence (session advisory lock on a direct
  connection) with a filesystem fallback for single-instance use.
- Fail-closed security: missing auth secret refuses requests; production refuses a
  live PayPal host, a mock settlement, or a missing database.
- Per-identity rate limiting on every money-bearing route, with a shared counter
  (PostgreSQL) so the limit is not spent once per instance.

## Important limitations

- **Sandbox only.** The demo moves no real money; the client is configured for the
  PayPal Sandbox host and a sandbox-only guard can hard-refuse a live host.
- **No independent security audit or certification.** Security controls are
  implemented and tested but have not been audited by a third party.
- **The verifier is a model plus deterministic checks.** It is not a formal
  correctness proof of a deliverable.
- **Customer self-service accounts and transactional email are implemented but
  disabled by default** because they require a verified email sending domain.
- **No wallet or fiat payout logic.** PACT does not hold funds itself; PayPal does.

## Installation

```bash
git clone https://github.com/itzebe/pact
cd pact/backend
uv venv --python 3.11 .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"
cp ../.env.example ../.env
export PACT_AUTH_SECRET="$(python -c 'import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))')"
uvicorn pact.main:app --reload --port 8000
```

See [docs/development.md](https://github.com/itzebe/pact/blob/master/docs/development.md) for the frontend and the test suites.

## Frequently asked questions (short)

- **Does PACT hold money?** No. PayPal holds it; PACT coordinates the escrow.
- **Is it real money?** No. The demo runs on the PayPal **Sandbox** host.
- **Can the AI authorize a payment?** No. The model proposes prices and verdicts; the
  settlement engine decides and the PayPal client moves the funds.
- **What if a webhook is repeated?** It is applied at most once (event id claimed in
  a shared store); a duplicate is acknowledged and ignored.
- **What if PayPal times out?** The job is marked `unresolved` and must be
  reconciled by reading PayPal; it is never retried blindly.

Full answers: [docs/faq.md](https://github.com/itzebe/pact/blob/master/docs/faq.md).
